GC65.status: Refined formal target; invariant-manifold existence unproved
GC65.model: Fix the real Swift–Hohenberg flow \(u_t=2u-(1+\Delta)^2u-u^3\) on \(\mathbb T^2=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^2\), initial \(u_0\in H^2(\mathbb T^2;\mathbb R)\). For each integer \(N\ge1\), \(P_N\) projects to \(|k|\le N\), and \(Q_N=I-P_N\).
GC65.canonical: Determine whether there exist \(N\) and a globally Lipschitz graph \(\Phi:P_NH^2\to Q_NH^2\) such that \(\mathcal M=\{p+\Phi(p)\}\) is forward invariant and attracts every bounded \(B\subset H^2\) exponentially: \(\operatorname{dist}_{H^2}(S(t)B,\mathcal M)\le C_Be^{-\lambda t}\) for \(t\ge0\), with \(\lambda>0\) uniform in B. This is an inertial-manifold problem, stronger than a finite-dimensional attractor.
GC65.resolution: Prove explicit N, spectral gap/cone invariance and graph tracking estimates in H², or prove no such graph exists for the frozen flow and Fourier cutoffs.

GC82.status: Provisional analytic solution to frozen coercivity inequality
GC82.model: Let \(m>0,\alpha\ge0\), \(u\in H^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)\) with \(M(u)=\|u\|_2^2=m\), \(E_{\alpha,1}(u)=\|(\Delta+1)u\|_2^2-\frac12\|u\|_4^4+\frac13\|u\|_6^6+\alpha\|K_1(u)\|_2^2\). Use the Bessel \(H^2\) norm \(\int(1+|\xi|^2)^2|\widehat u|^2\,d\xi\).
GC82.canonical: The claimed coercivity estimate holds, with constants independent of \(\alpha\ge0\): \(\boxed{E_{\alpha,1}(u)\ge\frac12\|u\|_{H^2}^2-\frac{67}{16}m}\). Indeed, for \(s=|u|^2\), \(-\frac12s^2+\frac13s^3\ge-\frac3{16}s\). Moreover \((1+t)^2\le2(1-t)^2+8\) for \(t=|\xi|^2\), so \(\|u\|_{H^2}^2\le2\|(\Delta+1)u\|_2^2+8m\). The curvature term is nonnegative. These identities answer the precise v1 yes/no question for all fixed masses.
GC82.resolution: Independently check the two pointwise inequalities and Fourier normalization, and, if demanded by the GC proof contract, formalize the exact uniform coercivity statement in Lean. Treat stronger optimal-constant or vanishing-regularizer estimates as new questions.

milestones: Verify the algebraic lower bound (-s^2/2+s^3/3ge-3s/16) for all (sge0).

GC82.notes: This proves fixed-mass coercivity, not coercivity uniformly over unrestricted mass and not strict binding. It does not prove compactness modulo translations.

GC103.status: Provisional analytic solution to frozen free resolvent exponent
GC103.model: On \(L^2(\mathbb R^2)\), \(H_0=(\Delta+1)^2\) with domain \(H^4\). Fix \(w(x)=\langle x\rangle^{-3}\), \(0<\kappa<1\), \(R_\kappa=(H_0+\kappa)^{-1}\), \(N(\kappa)=\|wR_\kappa w\|_{L^2\to L^2}\).
GC103.canonical: For this **free** shifted bi-Laplacian, the sharp growth exponent is \(p=1/2\): there are \(0<c<C<\infty\) with \(c\kappa^{-1/2}\le N(\kappa)\le C\kappa^{-1/2}\) for sufficiently small \(\kappa>0\). For \(h=wf\), the quadratic form is \(\int |\widehat h(\xi)|^2/((1-|\xi|^2)^2+\kappa)\,d\xi\). Since \(xw\) is bounded, \(\widehat h\in H^1_\xi\); uniform Fourier-circle trace estimates bound the shell integral above by \(C\kappa^{-1/2}\|f\|_2^2\), with the complement bounded. Choose a compactly supported f with nonzero Fourier trace of wf on \(|\xi|=1\) to obtain the matching lower bound. Hence \(\lim_{\kappa\downarrow0}\log N(\kappa)/\log(1/\kappa)=1/2\).
GC103.resolution: Supply a full weighted Fourier-circle trace lemma and explicit nonzero trial function, including constants and treatment away from the circle. Prove sharp bounds, or identify a gap in the proposed argument; a perturbed V or different weight is a separate question.

GC105.status: Provisional analytic solution for frozen linear spectral coefficient
GC105.model: Fix \(H_0=(\Delta+1)^2\) on \(L^2(\mathbb R^2)\), spectral value \(\lambda=1\), \(g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)\), and \(\Gamma(g)=\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\operatorname{Im}\langle g,(H_0-1-i\eta)^{-1}g\rangle\). Use the **unitary** 2D Fourier transform \(\widehat g=(2\pi)^{-1}\int e^{-ix\cdot\xi}g(x)\,dx\).
GC105.canonical: The frozen coefficient has an explicit nonnegative expression: \(\boxed{\Gamma(g)=\frac{\pi}{4}\int_0^{2\pi}|\widehat g(\sqrt2\,e_\theta)|^2\,d\theta+\frac{\pi^2}{4}|\widehat g(0)|^2}\). Indeed, polar integration with \(t=|\xi|^2\) gives multiplier denominator \(t(t-2)-i\eta\) and measure \(d\xi=\frac12\,dt\,d\theta\). The ordinary circle root t=2 contributes the first term; the collapsed point t=0 is an endpoint root and contributes the **half-weight** second term. Hence \(\Gamma(g)>0\) iff \(\widehat g(0)\ne0\) or the restriction to the circle \(|\xi|=\sqrt2\) is not identically zero. Any nonnegative nonzero compact bump g gives \(\widehat g(0)>0\).
GC105.resolution: Check the endpoint Poisson-kernel limit and constants rigorously for every smooth compactly supported g. This solves a linear spectral-density exercise only; a nonlinear Fermi golden rule damping theorem requires a separately frozen coherent state and coupling.
